evidence: Wikipedia's article on Taylor Swift: at 11 she visited Nashville record labels with demo tapes of Dolly Parton and Dixie Chicks karaoke covers; all of them rejected her, which led her to concentrate on songwriting.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Both are country songs written by a teenage girl about her own life, plainly told, with a story you can follow line by line. Listen for the detail: Parton's coat, Swift's porch and car radio. The pairing is our reading; the documented part is the demo tape.

explanation: When Taylor Swift was 11, she took tapes of herself singing Dolly Parton songs to record companies in Nashville. They all turned her down, so she started writing her own songs. It is documented as a starting point, not as a specific musical debt. Like Parton, Swift became famous as a songwriter first and kept control of her work.
